A delivery van leaves the station and must deliver to every zone below. All stops in a zone are delivered together, so you only choose the order of the zones. The order of stops inside each zone is decided separately.

How to read this: drivers at a station are creatures of habit. The history below counts what this station's drivers actually did with these same zones, and it is the strongest evidence you have: follow the usual first zone and the usual next-zone moves wherever they are consistent, and use the most similar past routes to settle the overall sweep. Zone IDs are hierarchical (e.g. `A-2.3B` = area A-2, row 3, column B); drivers usually finish one area before moving to the next and sweep neighbouring rows and columns in order. Fall back on travel times only where the history is silent or contradictory.
